text:
Maya (Marketing): Quick sync — post-launch redirect prioritization. We got a bunch of incoming links from the webinar and a couple of old blog anchors that point to deprecated pages. Need a short ops plan: how do we decide which redirects to run first (and whether 302 vs 301)?
Sam (SEO): Agree. Proposing "anchor velocity" as our main priority signal: how many unique referring pages/anchors appeared in the last 7 days. High velocity + high click-through => top priority.
Leo (Analytics): Data check: top 40 anchors from the webinar drove 68% of organic clicks last 14 days. I can export anchor -> clicks -> ctr -> landing page.
Olivia (Content): For the pages we redirect, we also need a canonical + schema sanity check. Some pages have FAQ schema that should be moved to the destination.
Jin (Web Dev): Ops question — what's the proposed format for the list? CSV mapping old_url,new_url,reason,owner,priority? I can wire a small script to push to the redirect tool.
Sam (SEO): Yes CSV like `old_url,new_url,anchor_velocity,clicks,priority` is perfect. Priority = high/med/low computed from rules. Also: use 302 for initial testing for 48–72h, then convert to 301 once metrics stable.
redirect-bot: automated crawl report: 52 deprecated URLs found by sitemap diff. Sample: `/integrations/old-connector -> /integrations/new-connector` (anchors: 23 recent). Full CSV on GCS: gs://redwood-marketing/redirects/1774601234-scan.csv
Maya (Marketing): Nice. Can Leo attach the top anchors CSV? We need to mark owner for every redirect so content can merge schemas.
Leo (Analytics): Attached in the drive link: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/abc123 (exports: anchors.csv, clicks.csv). I flagged top50 by velocity.
Olivia (Content): I'll own any redirect where the source page has unique copy we want to preserve or merge. Otherwise low-effort straight redirect to new landing. Also: for pages with FAQ schema, copy the JSON-LD to destination and update `@id` canonicals.
Jin (Web Dev): Quick implementation snippet for Netlify/_redirects or Cloudflare Worker (example):
```
# CSV mapping example (automated import)
/old-path-1,/new-path-1,anchor_vel=34,clicks=120,high
/old-path-2,/product,anchor_vel=5,clicks=8,low
```
# Cloudflare Worker pseudo
addEventListener('fetch', event => {
  const url = new URL(event.request.url)
  if (redirectMap[url.pathname]) {
    return event.respondWith(Response.redirect(redirectMap[url.pathname], 302))
  }
  return event.respondWith(fetch(event.request))
})
```
Jin (Web Dev): I'll queue the top20 (high) as 302s tomorrow morning, monitor for 72h, then swap to 301 if no regressions. Need confirmation on audit checks we run during trial.
Sam (SEO): Monitor: organic clicks, impressions, avg position, and crawl errors. Also run a quick lighthouse / structured-data test on destination pages for schema integrity. If CTR or position drops >10% after 72h, revert.
Maya (Marketing): Timeline: tomorrow import top20 as 302. Olivia to merge schema bits before we flip to 301. Jin to post a follow-up thread with the deploy diff. Leo to report delta after 72h.
Olivia (Content): I'll start merging FAQ schema for the top10 destinations today — will ping when done.
Leo (Analytics): I'll set up a 72h dashboard widget: clicks/imprs/ctr/position + a simple delta vs baseline.
Sam (SEO): One more note — update sitemap and canonical tags on destination (point to destination) before switching to 301 so search engines see the final mapping promptly.
Maya (Marketing): Perfect. Owners: Jin = deploy, Olivia = content/schema, Leo = metrics, Sam = validation rules. I'll coordinate comms to CS + Sales in case any anchors are high-intent leads. :thumbsup:
Jin (Web Dev): Will create the PR and tag everyone. Expect deploy window tomorrow 9am PT.
redirect-bot: deploy scheduled: 1774687634 by jin-webdev (302s for top20).
Maya (Marketing): Thanks team — will follow up in the deploy thread.
